scope: Czech and Slovak supplemental discovery only. The pass distinguishes named operating systems from their host computers, known clone relationships, and uncertain implementation families; no system records are created by this file.

candidates.reason: Czechoslovak microcomputer operating-system implementation documented by the SAPI historical site; independent sources describe it as the locally widespread CP/M-derived system. Retain it separately from upstream CP/M.
JSEP historical documentation names OS-10 EC as the operating system for the EC 1010. It is a system identity tied to a computer line, not the EC 1010 hardware itself.
JSEP documentation identifies MOS EC as the small operating system developed at VÚMS for EC 1021. Do not conflate it with similarly named MOS systems or later Unix experiments.
The Czechoslovak JSEP source identifies DOS EC as a disk operating-system line with named variants. Catalog the family once, with variants retained as releases rather than separate systems.
JSEP historical documentation identifies OS EC as the large multiuser operating-system line outside EC 1010 and EC 1021. Numbered forms are variants, not independent candidate identities.
SMEP documentation identifies PLOS-RV as a diskless real-time operating system. It is distinct from the non-real-time PLOS entry, which is not promoted here without further identity research.
Czech and Slovak historical sources describe DIAMS as a multiuser, dialog-oriented database operating system for SMEP systems. It is a software identity, not a database or SMEP hardware model.
SMEP documentation identifies DOS RV as a disk operating system for real-time tasks; Slovak VÚVT material specifically records DOS RV 3. Treat the numeral as a release/version.

The SMEP source groups the names as multitasking, multiuser systems and specifically calls FODOS an RT-11 clone. Verify whether they are separate systems, names of a shared implementation family, or compatibility modes before record creation.
The SMEP source calls RV OS a multitasking multiuser RSX-11 clone. It may warrant a derivative system record, but provenance and whether it is a port versus a local clone remain unverified.

The SMEP source describes RTE-II as a modified OS for M-6000, M-7000, and SM-1 machines built on HP-2000-compatible computers. Determine its relationship to the already cataloged HP RTE family before treating it as distinct.
SMEP and JSEP are regional computer-system programs and hardware families, not operating-system identities; their named OS components are recorded separately above.
